overview: Ridgway was the headquarters and northern terminal of the Rio Grande Southern, which began building from the town around 1890 toward Telluride, Ophir, Rico, and Durango.

The historic operating complex combined a passenger-and-freight depot, corporate and dispatch functions, a five-bay roundhouse, 50-foot turntable, boiler house, coaling structures, blacksmith and paint shops, sand and ice houses, and associated yard tracks.

moreHistory: The original depot survives after relocation, while the present museum area includes modern interpretive or reconstructed railroad features that must not be described as entirely original 1890 fabric.
Treat the yard, shops, roundhouse footprint, moved depot, and museum interpretation as related but distinct components.
